name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: I think we should focus on reviewing our prompts first, because they have the biggest impact on the quality of our outputs. By improving our prompts, we can increase the chances of getting accurate and relevant information, which is essential for our goal of self-improvement. I'm accepting the trade-off of potentially spending more time on prompt review, which might delay our progress on other areas like engine and routing improvements. This is a worthwhile investment, in my opinion, because well-crafted prompts lay the foundation for all our other improvements to build upon.

name: Gauge
text: Gauge: I hear the appeal of prompt tuning, but the real risk is that we’re optimizing for *output quality* while ignoring whether the system even *needs* better prompts to improve itself. What if the bottleneck is actually in the routing logic or the engine’s ability to act on feedback? Settle this by running a quick experiment: measure how much prompt tweaks improve the *next iteration* of the system versus tweaking the routing layer first—then we’ll know where to focus.
